text.p: Regional utility Irkutskenergo said on Tuesday its financial results in the first half of this year were unsatisfactory.

Irkutskenergo made a loss before tax of $13.70 million on sales of $435.47 million, according to unaudited figures prepared to international auditing standards. Comparisons for the first half of 1995 were not available.

Irkutskenergo blamed the loss on government-imposed limits in the second quarter of this year on increases in electricity charges, aggravated by a sharp rise in coal prices, and on a fall in the amount of electricity supplied to the wholesale energy market.

But a decision by the regional electricity commission to raise average charges for electricity by 37 percent and for heating by 10 percent in the fourth quarter of this year should compensate for this, it said in a statement.

An agreement on settling debts owed to Irkutskenergo by national utility UES (Unified Energy System) for energy supplies is a step forward, and so an agreement on the basis of future supplies to the wholesale market, it said.
"Irkutskenergo hopes for a further strengthening and development of business relations with UES," it said.

The two companies have been in a dispute above the ownership of three lucrative hydro-electric power stations now operated by Irkutskenergo, and UES also has its eyes on the 40 percent government stake in Irkutskenergo.
Irkutskenergo is one of only two Russian utilities fully independent from UES, which owns Russia's electricity grid and has 49-100 percent stakes in 68 of its 71 local power companies, or "energos".
Irkutskenergo is preparing a an issue of level-one American Depositary Receipts, which it expects to go ahead next month.
It is one of the most liquid Russian shares, and one of only a handful to have prepared accounts to international standards.
